set.st: Tom Kelly, a miserly Irish lead miner, smelted his own ore from a cave on the bluff and never trusted banks. After he died (1867) his heirs dug between $4,000 and $5,000 in gold from the ground under his hut, and further caches turned up later; local tradition says much more was never found. Detectorists still report scattered gold coins on the wooded bluff side. Laird (1927) repeats the local account that about 1868 a boy found $3,300 in gold eagles in cans at Kelly's old cabin. A 1936 WPA 'Iowa Oddities' piece lists four finds on the bluff: a $10,000 iron chest (Geiger and Becke), a $1,200 can (the boy Peter Fortune), an $1,800 small chest (a youth named Reynolds) and $500 found by workmen digging a reservoir on the old claim in 1914. It says a large iron chest Kelly had a Dubuque blacksmith forge (2 ft 10 in x 32 in x 8 in) has never been found and is believed to hold most of the fortune, and that augers were still probing in 1936. It gives his death as 15 May 1859, and the 1914 wire says c.1873; the card keeps 1867 from the heirs' find reported in Sept 1868. The 1914 find itself (Des Moines Register, 8 Sep 1914): workmen excavating for the new city reservoir on the bluff plowed up about $150 in silver on 6 Sep 1914, half dollars and quarters none later than 1860 and one of 1811; a crowd scrambled for it and police guarded the dig. So the WPA's '$500 in 1914' is this $150 in silver, inflated. The wire says Kelly lived in a 'shanty, half cave'.
set.pl: Kelly's Bluff, Dubuque: the round 1914 city reservoir site on the bluff top (1930 ortho, 2020 lidar)
pinev: 1914 reservoir dig on the bluff per the Des Moines Register (8 Sep 1914); a round structure about 40 m across at 42.4944,-90.6726 (with a second circle just S in 1930) is the only reservoir-shaped feature on the bluff top on the 1930 Iowa ortho and 2020 lidar.
